 An election worker at the voting center at City Hall on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, in Chula Vista, CA, prepares voting stickers for voters. (Nelvin C. Cepeda / The San Diego Union-Tribune)
 By U T Readers PUBLISHED: November 17, 2026 at 11:00 AM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Voting is one of the most important rights Americans have, yet finding time to exercise that right can be difficult. As a college student, I believe Election Day should become a federal holiday to make voting more accessible.
 Many Americans must balance work, school and family responsibilities, making it challenging to prioritize voting. While early voting and mail-in ballots provide alternatives, access to these options varies across states.
 An Election Day holiday would recognize the importance of civic participation and encourage more Americans to vote. Of course, a federal holiday would not guarantee everyone a day off, especially essential workers. However, it could be an important step alongside other efforts to improve voting accessibility.
 Regardless of political affiliation, we should all support making democratic participation more accessible.
 — Jillian Romeo, San Diego
